chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no servant who conceals goodness except that the days will not pass until Allah manifests goodness to him; and there is no servant who conceals evil except that the days will not pass until Allah manifests evil to him'.
ai.seo_question: What happens to secret good and evil deeds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the inevitability of divine recompense for both secret good and secret evil, reinforcing the concept of 'Istidraj' for hidden sins and 'Barakah' for hidden virtues. This teaching serves as a spiritual check against hypocrisy, reminding believers that God's observation transcends public perception, a key theme in Shia ethics regarding sincerity (Ikhlas).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sindy, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is none from a servant who does a good deed secretly except that the days would not pass by until Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Manifests goodness to him; and there is none from a servant who does an evil deed secretly except that the days would not go by until Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Manifests the evil to him’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih ibn Sindy from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Ali ibn abu Hamza from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said, ‘Whenever a servant (of Allah) does a good deed secretly, not very long thereafter Allah uncovers for him good rewards. Whenever a servant (of Allah) does an evil deed secretly, very shortly thereafter Allah uncovers for him an evil return and misfortune.’”
